chunks: And from him, from Al-Nadhr, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The hour during which supplication is answered on Friday is the time between the Imam's completion of the sermon until the people are evenly arranged in the rows, and another hour is from the end of the day until the setting of the sun.
ai.seo_question: What are the specific times on Friday when du'a is accepted according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights two distinct windows of divine responsiveness on Friday: the immediate post-sermon interval and the final moments before sunset. In Shia jurisprudence, the first period is often associated with the transition from the Imam's khutbah to the congregational prayer, while the second aligns with the time of Asr prayer, emphasizing the spiritual potency of these specific temporal markers in devotional practice.

en.hubeali:
And from him, from Al Nazar Bin Suweyd, from Abdullah Bin Sinan, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘The timing during which the supplication is Answered is the day of Friday what is between the prayer leader being free from the sermon, up to him evening out the people in the rows; and another timing is from the end of the day to the setting of the sun’.
en.sarwar: 4. The narrator of previous Hadith has also narrated from al-Nadr from ‘Abd Allah ibn Sinan who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘

The hour of Friday wherein prayers are answered is the time when the prayer leader completes the sermons, until people get ready in rows for Salah (prayer). The other hour is the time at the end of the day to sunset.’”
